recipes.name: Spooky Witches' Fingers
ingredients_raw: 1 (.75-ounce) tube red decorating food gel, or as needed

steps.text: Beat butter, confectioners' sugar, egg, almond extract, and vanilla extract together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until smooth. Gradually beat in flour, baking powder, and salt until combined. Wrap dough in plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 20 to 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Lightly grease baking sheets.

Scoop 1 heaping teaspoon of dough at a time onto a piece of waxed paper; keep remaining dough in the refrigerator. Roll dough into a thin finger-shaped cookie using the waxed paper. Press 1 almond into one end of cookie to give the appearance of a long fingernail. Squeeze cookie near the tip and near the center to give the impression of knuckles. You can also cut into dough with a sharp knife at the same points to give a more finger-like appearance. Repeat with remaining dough. Arrange shaped cookies on the prepared baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until cookies are slightly golden in color, 20 to 25 minutes.
Remove almonds from ends of each cookie; squeeze a small amount of red decorating gel into cavities. Replace almond to cause jam to ooze out around tips of cookies.

raw_recipe.headline: Spooky Witches' Fingers
raw_recipe.description: This spooky witches' fingers recipe uses a homemade cookie dough decorated with red jam and almonds for bloody fingernails for a tasty Halloween treat.

video.description: See how to make scary-good Halloween cookies that look like witches’ fingers.

review.reviewBody: I made these cookies for my son's school party and they were a great hit. We added green food coloring to the dough and when I took them out of the oven I added a single chocolate chip for a wart. We also added red gel food coloring for the severed end of the finger. The cookies do enlarge when baked (almost double the thickness) so make sure you don't make them to round when you are rolling them out. The cookie flavor was good on top of looking great, thanks for a fun recipe.

You know how frustrating it is to pull that last half inch of waxed paper off the roll right in the middle of a recipe?! If this happens to you, it IS worth the trip to the store--I handled the first batch too much and they melted pretty flat in the oven. For a second batch, it worked really well to use a glass baking dish to squish the dough to about half an inch thick between two sheets of waxed paper to chill (for closer to an hour--20-30 minutes wasn't quite enough). Then I cut "french fries" that I could pull out of the fridge 2 or 3 at a time and quickly roll into finger shape--saves time and the less handling the better! Mine also got a bonus hour in the fridge before baking (my family decided they needed dinner), which helped keep them firm. I colored half the dough green and the other half purple, and gave each finger a wart or two of the opposite color. I mixed red food coloring with chocolate syrup and coated the almonds in that before placing them on the gel. Then I added red sugar sprinkles to the colored syrup for texture and dipped the "severed" ends into that. I was really pleased with the results--very gory! Last but not least, adults raved about how delicious they were, and the kids liked them but weren’t quite as crazy about them—they aren’t overly sweet.

These cookies were fantastic for our sons' daycare Halloween party. All the children and the staff loved them and there were no leftovers come pick-up time. I skipped the red food coloring and went with raspberry jam to hold the "nails" on. The two cautions I will offer, as some other reviewers did, is 1) that you have to roll out the fingers SMALL and THIN or you'll get monster fingers--a raw cookie the length and thickness of your pinky will be the size of your middle finger upon baking--and 2) the salt is better left out, or you'll also get monster fingers. They will rise just fine, look and taste perfect without the salt.

These were so much fun to make! Between batches in the oven, I put the cookie sheet in the refrigerator. I think it helps them keep their shape. I also used toasted almonds for their great flavor and strawberry jam. 🎃

I loved this recipe! It was exactly what I was looking for. I made mine too look like zombie fingers for our Zombie themed Halloween party. I used the raspberry jam, which was perfect for the blood under the almonds. I used red, green, yellow, and black gel icing for the cookies, after they were cooked and cooled. I also added the green food coloring with the wet ingredients, before adding the dry. I siffted the dry ingredients, so I had to add additional flour, maybe a 1/3 cup. Also, I used 1/2 cup powder sugar and 1/2 cup granulated sugar. 
This will be my go to recipe from here on out.

I made these twice. The first time they were very bland and a bit salty, and spread into more like ogre toes than witch fingers. The second time we added sliced almond nails, spirulina green food coloring, doubled both the almond and vanilla extract, and omitted the leavening agent. They were much improved the second time even without additional sugar. Be mindful of baking time and remove as they get very lightly browned, otherwise they will be dry. I have made witch fingers before with a mandelhöernchen cookie dough when I have marzipan on hand and I think I prefer that version, however this version came together very quickly and might be more palatable for kids especially if you make them more flavorful by increasing the extracts.

These were so very cute and easy to make. I used sliced almonds for the nails and sort of slid them into the dough a bit. I also tinted the dough green. I did NOT grease the pan, I prefer to use silicon baking liners. When I took them out of the oven I immediately removed the almond slices, added a squeeze of red gel and replaced the almosn slice "nail". I arranged them on a platter lined with easter basket grass. In addition I dipped pretzel logs in melted white chocolate and called them "dead mans bones" and placed those on the same platter. Next time I am planning on trying a strawberry jelly dot or raspberry under the almond.

great base recipe. I did make changes based on the other reviews. I put 3/4 cup confectioners sugar plus 1/4 cup granulated sugar to add sweetness. I also used two tablespoons of vanilla instead of almond since I was making these for my nephews. I dipped the almond slices in strawberry preserves so it would ooze out when I applied the "nail tips" prior to baking. I also recommend leaving the dough in fridge at least 30 mins and working with small portions of dough at a time. I baked less than the time on recipe, maybe 15 mins or until slightly golden. The cookies came out so delicious and soft on the inside. I then went back with a little red frosting gel around the cuticles and the end of fingers! So fun and creepy!!

I make these every year. They always spread a bit more than I remember, but no matter what imperfections I see, people always love them. 
I use the tip of a butter knife to make the impression where the fingernail will go, then add a sliced almond onto a drop of frosting after baking. 
This year I didn't want to send anyone to the market, Covid and all, so instead of red frosting I used some raspberry jam I made over the summer. THE RASPBERRY JAM LOOKS AMAZING!!! It's a bit chunky, and a darker red than the strawberry I had. I'm never going back to frosting - always jam from now on!

I've made this recipe the last 2 years as is, and has been a hit both at family parties and at work. For an additional creepy factor, I took some slivered almonds, and pushed one or two of them halfway into the end of the finger opposite the "nail".This makes the fingers look like the severed, cracked bones are sticking out of the end. Really effective when you add the red food coloring to give it the appearance of blood. I appreciate the tip of gluing the almond to the end with a bit of jam, since some of my "fingernails" came off when it came time to present and serve the cookies. I will try that tirick next time I make these. Great recipe, so glad I found this! :-) :-) :-)

Love this recipe. I amped up the “ick” factor by adding a short length of pretzel at the severed end with some strawberry jam. I also used sliced almonds instead of whole almonds for a more realistic fingernail. These were applied with a little strawberry dab prior to baking (like the pretzels) so the jam will coagulate nicely. This also eliminates having to remove and reapply the nails post-bake. Also, add a few toes in there for good measure. When your friends and family refuse to eat them because they are too gross you have it about right.

My friend and I make these every year for Halloween......makes a great tradition for us. Plan to try the recipe for Christmas cookies using.......all almond extract, no vanilla....round dollops for the cookie....jarred cherry in the middle!

the dryest morsels I have had the displeasure of putting in my mouth.The bland shortbread had no almond taste even though I added extra extract because I thought the amount was too little. the closest thing to this would be eating dehydrated sand while sniffing an almond. do not make.

Time consuming? Yes. Cuted and delicious definitely YES! I read most reviews before proceeding and swapped almond extract for vanilla, almonds for shredded almonds, used just a pinch of salt and powdered sugar as directed, which was sweet for me so definitely don't recommend adding more sugar as some reviews point. Also, followed multiple advice to roll fingers thin but they ended up too thin for me, next time will make them a tad thicker. Took 17 minutes for the cookies to be fully ready. I also made the dough the night before and added green color. The dough was hard rock in the am so I let it sit room temperature for 1.5 hours before rolling the cookies. I also used 3/4 cup of butter as I didn't have enough and it turned out fine. Definitely going to make again.

Followed the recipe exactly and it works just like that! Even for novice baker! A couple tips from me: Fastest to just roll the doughs between my palms and giving it the knuckle-bumps at the same time. For optimal strawberry oozing, use the almond to scoop out the jam, it will be just enough to hold it in place.
Too much butter or too little flour perhaps, so fingers flattened too much. 13-15 mins is more than enough in the oven.

I have been making this recipe for years for my Halloween party and they are a huge hit! They are a perfect butter cookie. You do have to make them smaller than you think since the dough expands when baking, but overall such a yummy cookie!

Absolutely SCRUMPTIOUS!! These buttery cookie fingers were easy to make (even for this self-proclaimed non-baker!)! They turned out a little larger than I had hoped, but they still look oh so festive!
Need to make them much thinner as they grow in size as they bake. I used raspberry jam to add blood effect and flavour.
Perfect recipe I Itried it with pre-made cookie dough and they didn't keep it sshap.This recipe was great taste good
